cues.zh: 好，现在……来谈认知能力。嗯……
cues.en: Okay, now... down to cognitive ability. Well...

cues.zh: 你该如何界定智力？
cues.en: How can you conceptualize intelligence?

cues.zh: 嗯，这是个大问题，因为你最初的界定
cues.en: Well, this is a major problem, because your initial conceptualization

cues.zh: 在一定程度上决定了你将采用什么策略
cues.en: determines, in part, the strategies that you're going to use

cues.zh: 去研究智力。而且……
cues.en: to investigate intelligence. And...

cues.zh: 当你说……当你把一句话精简成“什么是智力？”时……
cues.en: when you say... when you pare a sentence down to "What is intelligence?"...

cues.zh: ——这句话就有问题了，因为其中一部分是在问
cues.en: - the sentence is problematic, because part of it is a question about

cues.zh: “这种东西是否以及如何能在世界上显现出来？”
cues.en: "if and how such a thing might manifest itself in the world?"

cues.zh: 确实存在一个事实——或一组事实——对应着智力
cues.en: There's a fact out there -or set of facts- that corresponds to intelligence

cues.zh: 但另一个问题是，你说“智力”时到底*指*什么？
cues.en: but the other problem is, well, what do you *mean* when you say "intelligence"?

cues.zh: 你得把这一点确定下来，如果你想要
cues.en: And you kinda have to nail that down, if you're gonna have

cues.zh: 进行一场不至于完全跑偏的关于智力的对话。
cues.en: a conversation about intelligence that doesn't go entirely astray.

cues.zh: 所以既有定义问题，也有实证问题。
cues.en: And so you've got a definitional problem as well as an empirical problem.

cues.zh: 所以……
cues.en: And so...

cues.zh: 曾经有过——这在20世纪90年代尤其明显——
cues.en: There have been -and this was especially true in the 1990s-

cues.zh: 人们从20世纪20年代起就在研究智力，IQ智力，
cues.en: People have been studying intelligence, IQ intelligence, since the 1920s

cues.zh: 这是心理学中一个非常成熟的分支。
cues.en: and it's a very well established branch of psychology.

cues.zh: 关于IQ研究，我必须告诉你的一点是，
cues.en: One of the things I have to tell you about it -IQ research- is that

cues.zh: 如果你不认可IQ研究，那你不妨把心理学的其余部分全都扔掉。
cues.en: if you don't buy IQ research, you might as well throw away all the rest of Psychology.

cues.zh: 原因在于……
cues.en: And the reason for that is that...

cues.zh: 首先，那些“开发”智力测试的心理学家，正是
cues.en: The psychologists, first of all, who "developed" intelligence testing, were among the

cues.zh: 早期心理学家中率先建立统计技术的人，而所有心理学家都用这些技术
cues.en: early psychologists who instantiated the statistical techniques that all psychologists use

cues.zh: 来验证和检验他们的所有假设。
cues.en: to verify and test all of their hypotheses.

cues.zh: 所以最后你会把婴儿和洗澡水一起倒掉。
cues.en: So you end up throwing the baby out with the bathwater.

cues.zh: 而“智商界的人”对智力的定义更为严格和精确
cues.en: And the "IQ people" have defined intelligence in a more stringent and accurate way

cues.zh: 比我们定义几乎任何其他心理学构念都更精确，所以……
cues.en: than we've been able to define almost any other psychological construct, and so...

cues.zh: 如果你把定义得最完善的那个扔掉
cues.en: if you toss out the one that's the most well defined

cues.zh: 那你就得面对一个问题：剩下那些你打算怎么办
cues.en: then you're kind of stuck with the problem of what are you going to do with all the ones that you have left over

cues.zh: 它们的定义远没有那么完善，测量也远没有那么精确，或者说……
cues.en: that are nowhere near as well defined or as well measured or as...

cues.zh: 或者说它们的预测效度要低得多，而且被证明的力度和清晰度也远远不够。
cues.en: or whose predictive validity is much less and has been demonstrated with much less vigor and clarity.

cues.zh: 不管怎样，尽管如此，
cues.en: Anyways, despite all that,

cues.zh: 人们还是提出了多种不同的智力
cues.en: people have posited a number of different intelligences

cues.zh: 而且这很合理，因为如果你把智力理解为……
cues.en: and reasonably so, because, if you think of intelligence as...

cues.zh: 那种能推动你在世界上成功前行的东西；
cues.en: that which might move you forward successfully in the world;

cues.zh: 显然，有相当多的现象
cues.en: obviously, there's a fair number of phenomena

cues.zh: 与可能归入这一范畴的个体相关联。
cues.en: that are associated with individuals that might fit into that category.

cues.zh: 所以我们有……
cues.en: So we have...

cues.zh: ……人们做出了这些区分。
cues.en: ... people have made these distinctions.

cues.zh: 比如，Bob Sternberg 区分了
cues.en: Bob Sternberg, for example, has distinguished between

cues.zh: 实用智力与分析智力
cues.en: practical vs analytical intelligence

cues.zh: 他倾向于把实用智力理解为“街头智慧”
cues.en: and he kind of thinks of practical as like "street smarts"

cues.zh: 并试图把它与分析智力分开，而后者
cues.en: and has attempted to dissociate that from the kind of analytical intelligence that

cues.zh: ……后者更能代表更纯粹的 IQ 研究。不过我认为他完全没有成功地做到这一点
cues.en: ...that characterizes more straight IQ research. I don't think he's done it successfully as well, at all

cues.zh: 而且自 1990 年代以来，人们对他提出的实用智力的兴趣急剧下降，因为……
cues.en: and since the 1990s interest in his practical intelligence has declined precipitously, because...

cues.zh: 当它与标准 IQ 智力正面比较时
cues.en: when it is matched head-to-head with standard IQ intelligence

cues.zh: IQ 智力吃掉了所有变异。
cues.en: the IQ intelligence eats up all the variability.

cues.zh: 就我目前所见，真正发生的情况是
cues.en: What's really happened, as far as I can tell so far, is that

cues.zh: 当我们试图预测人们的人生轨迹时
cues.en: when we're trying to predict people's course through life

cues.zh: IQ 做得非常好，然后还有一项特质也做得非常好
cues.en: IQ does a very good job, and then one of the traits does a very good job as well

cues.zh: 那就是尽责性
cues.en: which is conscientiousness

cues.zh: ——但它不如 IQ 做得好。
cues.en: - but it doesn't do as good a job as IQ.

cues.zh: 这可能部分是因为我们无法很好地衡量尽责性。
cues.en: Now, that partly might be because we can't measure conscientiousness very well.

cues.zh: 我们只能依赖自我报告，或者我可以收集别人对你的评价
cues.en: We're stuck with self reports or maybe I could gather peer reports about you

cues.zh: 或者我可以收集你父母对你的评价，或者老师的评价
cues.en: or I could gather your parents' reports about you, or teacher's reports

cues.zh: 而每一种评价似乎都能
cues.en: and each of those seems to

cues.zh: 多捕捉到一点这个模式，
cues.en: pick up a little bit more of the pattern,

cues.zh: 因为你自己了解自己，但别人了解你
cues.en: because you know yourself, but other people know you

cues.zh: 的方式和你了解自己的方式不同，而这其中仍然有一定的准确性。
cues.en: differently than you know yourself, and there's still some accuracy in that.

cues.zh: 你可以获取关于尽责性这类特质的多个评分者的报告，
cues.en: You can get multiple rater reports of something like conscientiousness,

cues.zh: 这会提高它的预测效度。
cues.en: and that will up its predictive validity.

cues.zh: 但归根结底，在尽责性上你能做到的最好程度
cues.en: But, in the final analysis, the best you seem to be able to do with conscientiousness

cues.zh: 大约是与长期绩效的0.4相关性，
cues.en: is about a .4 correlation with long term performance,

cues.zh: 而对于IQ，在复杂工作中，你可能达到0.5甚至0.6。
cues.en: whereas with IQ, in complex jobs, you can probably get .5 and maybe .6.

cues.zh: 所以0.5是变异量的25%——你要把它平方——0.6是变异量的36%
cues.en: So .5 is 25% of the variants -you're going to square it- .6 is 36% of the variants

cues.zh: 而0.4是变异量的16%。
cues.en: and .4 is 16% of the variants.

cues.zh: 所以即使在“低端”……比如说，尽责性的“高端”是0.4……也就是16%，
cues.en: So even at the "low end"... let's say, "high end" for conscientiousness is .4... or 16%,

cues.zh: 智商的“低端”是0.5，也就是25%，
cues.en: "Low end" for IQ is .5 or 25%,

cues.zh: 对智商的“低端”估计使其影响力是
cues.en: "Low end" estimates of IQ make it 1.5 times more powerful than

cues.zh: 对尽责性“高端”估计的1.5倍。
cues.en: the "high end" estimates of conscientiousness.

cues.zh: 我觉得这大致是对的。你会想“我们为什么还要争论这个”？
cues.en: And I think that's about right. You'd think "Why do we even have to debate this"?

cues.zh: 因为对我来说太明显了，智力是人生成功的主要预测因素；我是说……
cues.en: Because it's so bloody obvious to me that intelligence is a major predictor of life success; I mean...

cues.zh: 你们这些人——我测过多伦多大学的人的智商——你知道……
cues.en: You people - I've measured the IQ of University of Toronto people- you know...

cues.zh: 这个房间里智商低于120的人很罕见。
cues.en: People in this room who have an IQ of less than 120 are rare.

cues.zh: 但为什么呢？嗯……
cues.en: But why? Well...

cues.zh: 聪明人上大学……现在，这算是有争议的说法吗？
cues.en: Smart people go to University... now, is that actually a contentious statement?

cues.zh: 这不该是有争议的说法，这是不言自明的！
cues.en: Well it shouldn't be a contentious statement; it's self-evident!

cues.zh: 大学设立的初衷其实就是
cues.en: Universities are actually set up so that

cues.zh: 让聪明人能拓展自己的能力，这正是大学存在的意义！
cues.en: smart people could expand their abilities, that is why they were there!

cues.zh: 你是根据评估结果被选拔出来的，而这些评估本质上就是为了衡量类似智力的东西。
cues.en: You're selected on the basis of assessments that are essentially there to assess something like intelligence.

cues.zh: *来自学生的想法*
cues.en: *Idea from a Student*

cues.zh: 是的，但这正是争议的一部分——它*合理*吗？而这是个测量问题。
cues.en: Yes, but that is part of the controversy - is it *reasonable*? And this is a measurement issue.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么我一直在某种程度上教你心理测量学，因为
cues.en: And that's why I've been instructing you, to some degree, in Psychometrics, because

cues.zh: 我们其实知道怎么做，我们知道如何回答这个问题。
cues.en: we actually know how to do this, we know how to answer that question.

cues.zh: 那么，让我们来看看
cues.en: So, let's take a look at how

cues.zh: 智力是如何被评估的，以及为什么。
cues.en: intelligence has been assessed and why.

cues.zh: 然后，你可以自己做出判断。
cues.en: And then, you can make up your own mind.

cues.zh: 总之，这里有一些其他“形式”智力的例子。
cues.en: Anyways, here's some of the examples of other "forms" of intelligence.

cues.zh: 那么问题来了：拥有不同*形式*的智能意味着什么？
cues.en: And so, then the question is: what does it mean to have a different *form* of Intelligence?

cues.zh: A形式和B形式会完全不相关吗？
cues.en: Would Form A and Form B be completely uncorrelated?

cues.zh: 就像外向性和神经质那样？还是会略微相关？还是会……
cues.en: Like extroversion and say, neuroticism? Or would they be slightly correlated? Or would they be...

cues.zh: ……高度相关？然后你可能会问：它们得相关到什么程度……
cues.en: ... highly correlated? And then, you might ask: well, how highly correlated do they have to be...

cues.zh: ……才算同一种东西？
cues.en: ... before they're the same thing?

cues.zh: 或者，它们得有多不相关，才算不同的东西？
cues.en: Or, how uncorrelated do they have to be before they're different things?

cues.zh: 实际上，这个问题的答案归结为“实际效用”之类的东西。
cues.en: And actually, the answer to that comes down to something like "practical utility".

cues.zh: 就好比……想象我想弄清楚你在大学里会有多出色。
cues.en: It's like... imagine I'm trying to figure out how well you'll do in University.

cues.zh: 我测量了某样东西……它和我测量的关于你的另一样东西相关性达到0.7。
cues.en: And I measure one thing... and it's correlated at .7 with another thing I measure about you.

cues.zh: 那我可能会说“这两样东西是相同的，还是不同的？”它们相关性相当高……
cues.en: Well, then I might say "are those two things the same, or different?" They're pretty highly correlated...

cues.zh: ……你在一个方面高，意味着你在另一个方面也会高。
cues.en: ... your high on one means you're going to be high in the other.

cues.zh: 那么……同时测量这两者有什么用处吗？
cues.en: Well, so... is there any utility in measuring both things?

cues.zh: 而实际上，弄清楚这一点的方法是：从统计上做。
cues.en: And the way you figure that out, actually, is: you do it statistically.

cues.zh: 所以，我们取目标，可能是你在大学期间的表现。
cues.en: So, we take the target, which might be your performance across University.

cues.zh: 然后我们说：“那么，我们能否更好地预测你在大学期间的表现
cues.en: And then, we say: "Well, can we predict your performance across University better

cues.zh: 用一个变量？还是两个变量？”
cues.en: by using one variable? Or two variables?"

cues.zh: 所以，当你把两者都放入回归方程时——回归方程所做的就是：
cues.en: So, when you enter them both into a regression equation - all a regression equation does:

cues.zh: 很简单；你在试图预测一个目标……
cues.en: It's quite simple; So, you're trying to predict a target...

cues.zh: ……而回归方程告诉你：你能多好地预测那个目标……
cues.en: ... and the regression equation tells you: how well you can predict that target...

cues.zh: ……如果你知道另一个事实。
cues.en: ... if you know another fact.

cues.zh: 然后，这就变得有点复杂了，因为那是一种相关性：你能用A多好地预测B。
cues.en: Now, then it gets a little complicated, because that's a correlation: how well you can predict B with A.

cues.zh: 回归会说，如果你知道 A 和 B，你能多大程度预测 C……
cues.en: Well, a regression will say, how much you can predict C if you know A and B...

cues.zh: ……或者 A、B、C、D 和 E，因为你可以用多个预测变量……
cues.en: ... or A and B and C and D and E, because you can use multiple predictors...

cues.zh: ……还可以给它们加权，所以可能是 2×A + 1×B = C。
cues.en: ... and you can weigh them, so it might be 2xA + 1xB = C.

cues.zh: 回归方程做的就是这些；只是乘法和加法，非常非常简单。
cues.en: And that's all a regression equation does; It's just multiplication and addition, very very straightforward.

cues.zh: 所以，两个变量在功能上足够不同……
cues.en: And so, two variables are sufficiently different functionally...

cues.zh: ……前提是你能同时用它们来预测某个感兴趣的东西。
cues.en: ... if you can use both of them simultaneously to predict something of interest.

cues.zh: 所以再说一次，这是一种工具式的方法——心理测量学家就是这么做的。
cues.en: So again, it's a tool-like approach -this is how the psychometricians do it.

cues.zh: 它是真实存在的东西。
cues.en: It's something real.

cues.zh: 嗯，如果你能测量它，而且它能帮你预测，那它就是真实的。
cues.en: Well, it's real if you can measure it and it helps you predict.

cues.zh: 定义就是这样。那么，你可能会问：
cues.en: That's how it's defined. So, then you might say:

cues.zh: “存在这些多元智能吗？
cues.en: "Are there these multiple intelligences?

cues.zh: 那么，第一个问题是：“你说的*存在*是什么意思？”
cues.en: Well, the first question would be: "What do you mean by *are there*?"

cues.zh: 答案会是：“那好，让我们把问题明确一下。”因为我们要以科学的态度来对待它。
cues.en: And the answer to that would be: "Well, let's specify the question.", since we're going to be scientific about it.

cues.zh: 让我们预测人们在大学里的表现如何：我们先从一个假设开始：
cues.en: Let's predict how well people do in University: we'll start with the assumption that:

cues.zh: 如果智力与大学成功无关，那你谈论的很可能就不是智力。
cues.en: If intelligence isn't associated with University success, then you're probably not talking about intelligence.

cues.zh: 现在，你可以对此提出异议，对吧？
cues.en: Now, you could argue that, right?

cues.zh: 因为你可以说：“嗯，智力与大学成功毫无关系。”
cues.en: Because you could say: "Well, Intelligence has nothing to do with University success."

cues.zh: 但这是个定义问题！我们得先达成一致。
cues.en: But, that's a definitional matter! We'd have to agree to begin with.

cues.zh: 以这样的预设开始是否合理：智力……
cues.en: Is it reasonable to start with the presupposition that intelligence...

cues.zh: ……和大学成功有某些共同之处？
cues.en: ... and university success share something in common?

cues.zh: 嗯，我觉得否认这个初始命题的人一定是傻了；不过，你也可以否认……
cues.en: Well, I think you have to be daft to deny that initial proposition; although, you could...

cues.zh: 因为你可以说这是特权、社会经济地位，或者……
cues.en: Because you could say it was privilege, or socio-economic status, or...

cues.zh: ……任何数量的社会学现象，其中一些显然相关。
cues.en: ... any number of sociological phenomena, and some of those are obviously relevant.

cues.zh: 比如社会阶层……
cues.en: Social class, for example...

cues.zh: 因为，你知道，如果你处于较高的社会阶层
cues.en: Because, you know, if you're in a higher social class

cues.zh: 而且所有条件都相同，包括智力——
cues.en: and all things being equal, intelligence included -

cues.zh: ——如果你处于较高的社会阶层，你更有可能上大学
cues.en: - if you're in a higher social class, you're more likely to go into University

cues.zh: 相比处于较低社会阶层的情况。
cues.en: than you are if you were on a lower social class.

cues.zh: 所以，还有其他因素……
cues.en: So, there's other factors that...

cues.zh: ……会影响你在大学里是否表现出色……
cues.en: ... are going to influence whether or not you'll do well in University...

cues.zh: ……但我们会假设其中之一可能是智力。
cues.en: ... but we're going to assume that one of them might be intelligence.

cues.zh: 但是，然后你会问：“那么……”
cues.en: But, then you would ask: "Well..."

cues.zh: “……如果你测量社会智力……”
cues.en: "... if you measured social intelligence..."

cues.zh: （他们怎么称呼那个？）——“情商”；
cues.en: (What do they call that?) - "Emotional intelligence";

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，情商并不存在……
cues.en: which DOES NOT exist, by the way...

cues.zh: 情商、道德智力、语言智力、音乐智力、逻辑智力、数学智力……
cues.en: Emotional intelligence, Moral intelligence, Linguistic, Musical, Logical, Mathematical...

cues.zh: ……空间智力、身体动觉智力、内省智力和人际智力。
cues.en: ... Spacial, Body kinesthetic, Intrapersonal and Interpersonal.

cues.zh: 这些都是智力的不同形式。
cues.en: All different forms of intelligence.

cues.zh: 好，那么，要回答“它们是否存在”这个问题……
cues.en: Okay, so, to answer the question of "whether they exist"...

cues.zh: 你首先要做的是选一个目标——预测大学表现——
cues.en: What you do first is pick a target - prediction of university performance -

cues.zh: 然后，为每一项制定测量方法……
cues.en: then, you make a measure for each of them...

cues.zh: 接着，你要检验这个测量方法在多个实例中是否测的是同一个东西……
cues.en: Then, you test to see if the measure measured the same thing across multiple instances...

cues.zh: ……在同一个人身上；这是信度测试，因为……
cues.en: ... within the same person; that's a reliability test, because...

cues.zh: ……如果你的尺子一用就伸缩，那还有什么用？！
cues.en: ... what the hell good is your ruler if it stretches when you use it?!

cues.zh: ——它必须在多次测量中测出同一个东西——
cues.en: -It has to measure the same thing multiple times-

cues.zh: 然后，你会说：“好，我们把这些不同的智力都拿来，然后……”
cues.en: And then, you would say: "OK, we'll take all these different intelligences, and...

cues.zh: ……我们决定衡量它们的方式……
cues.en: ... the way we've decided to measure them...

cues.zh: ……我们要做的第一件事，就是看看它们之间的相关性有多高。
cues.en: ... the first thing we'll do is see how highly correlated they are.

cues.zh: 因为，如果它们是完整的——其中两个完全相关——那你就只有一个；
cues.en: Because, if they're complete - two of them are completely correlated - then you have one;

cues.zh: 你没有两个，因为这实际上就是一个而非两个的定义。
cues.en: You don't have two, because that's virtually the definition of one instead of two.

cues.zh: 你可以对它们做因子分析，看看能否提取出它们共有的东西；
cues.en: You can factor-analyze them and see if you can pull out what's common across all of them;

cues.zh: 那是另一回事，因为那时你可能会说：
cues.en: that's another thing, because then you might say:

cues.zh: “嗯，智力就是所有这些智力测量中共同的东西。”
cues.en: "Well, intelligence is what's common across all the measures of these intelligences."

cues.zh: 这是一个命题，不是事实！
cues.en: It's a proposition, it's not a fact!

cues.zh: 你得决定是否同意它。
cues.en: You have to decide if you're going to agree with it.

cues.zh: 但如果你要那么做，你会用因子分析，然后你会说：
cues.en: But, if you were going to do that, you'd use a factor analysis, and you'd say:

cues.zh: “嗯，如果某人更有可能在音乐方面有天赋，如果他们在语言能力上也很高……”
cues.en: "Well, if somebody was more likely to be Musical, if they were also high in Linguistic ability..."

cues.zh: “……并且更可能偏向逻辑和数学，如果他们有高空间能力等等。”
cues.en: "... and more likely to be logical and mathematically inclined, if they had a high spacial ability, etc."

cues.zh: 那么你就会假设所有这些表现背后有一个因素
cues.en: then you'd be hypothesising that there is one factor behind all of those manifestations

cues.zh: 在某种程度上是相似的；也许，根本没有！
cues.en: that's somehow similar; and maybe, there wouldn't be!

cues.zh: 然后，你会把你所有的测量数据放进类似多元回归分析的东西里……
cues.en: And then, you'd take all your measures and put them into something like a multiple regression analysis...

cues.zh: 然后你会预测你的目标——大学表现。
cues.en: and you'd predict your target - University performance.

cues.zh: 然后，也许你会说：“等一下——别只用大学表现”
cues.en: And then, maybe you'd say: "Wait a minute - let's not just *use* University performance"

cues.zh: “让我们用初中表现、高中表现、大学表现和工作成功！”
cues.en: "Let's use Junior-High performance, High-School performance, University performance and Job Success!"

cues.zh: 然后，假设唯一能预测所有这些类别中成功的东西……
cues.en: And then, let's say that the only things that predicts success across all those categories...

cues.zh: 而且，它们全都相同，我们将定义为智力——嗯，基本上这就是你最终得到IQ的方式。
cues.en: and, that are all the same, we are going to define as intelligence - well, that's basically how you end up with IQ.

cues.zh: 可以说，智商就是所有可能的智力测试中共同的部分。那么……
cues.en: You could say that IQ is what's common across all possible sets of intelligence tests. Now...

cues.zh: ……人们会争论这一点，因为……
cues.en: ... people are gonna debate that, because...

cues.zh: 你还是得定义什么才算是一项测试。
cues.en: you still have to define what constitutes a test.

cues.zh: 但心理测量学家们的处理方式，至少在某种程度上解决了这个问题，他们的说法是……
cues.en: But, the way the Psychometricians have managed it, and have taken care of this at least to some degree, is to say...

cues.zh: ……我们不会把所测量的一切都定义为智力。
cues.en: ... we're not going to define everything that we measure as intelligence.

cues.zh: 所以，外向的人在社交上更流利——还是说，我们要把这叫作智力？
cues.en: So, extroverted people are more socially fluent - or, are we going to call that intelligence?

cues.zh: 不！我们把这叫作“人格”。我们把这叫作“外向性”
cues.en: No! We're gonna call that "personality". We're gonna call that "extroversion"

cues.zh: 我们把这叫作压力耐受度。你可能会说，好吧……
cues.en: and we're gonna call stress-tolerance. You could say, well...

cues.zh: “如果你能承受更多压力，你就更聪明！”这就像是，不——我们不是这样定义的。
cues.en: "If you can tolerate more stress, you're more intelligent!" It's like, well, no - that isn't how we've defined it.

cues.zh: 我们把这定义为神经质程度较低。
cues.en: We're gonna define that as being lower in neuroticism.

cues.zh: 如果你乐于合作，你就更聪明——这就是“情商”。
cues.en: If you're cooperative, you're more intelligent - that's "emotional intelligence".

cues.zh: 那又怎样？如果你争强好胜，你就没那么聪明？不……
cues.en: Well, what? You're less intelligent if you're competitive? Well, no...

cues.zh: 所以我们把这归到宜人性上。那么问题可能是：
cues.en: So, we parse that off to agreeableness. So then the question might be:

cues.zh: “这些所谓的‘智力’还剩下什么……”
cues.en: "Is there anything left of these so-called 'intelligences'..."

cues.zh: “……一旦你控制了人格和智商？”答案是：没有！
cues.en: ".. once you control for personality and IQ?" and the answer is: NO!

cues.zh: 什么都没有。它们什么都没剩下！
cues.en: Nothing. Nothing left of them!

cues.zh: 而那些不断推销这些观念的人，还在继续推销……
cues.en: And the people who keep pushing these ideas, keep trying to push them...

cues.zh: 因为他们不喜欢真正的个体差异这个概念。
cues.en: because they don't like the idea of real individual differences.

cues.zh: 对我来说，这纯粹就是把脑袋埋进沙子里，因为很明显……
cues.en: And to me, that's just a matter of stickin' your damn head in the sand, because it's obvious...

cues.zh: 看吧：你即将有个孩子。
cues.en: Here: you're going to have a child.

cues.zh: 你想让孩子智商是65还是145？
cues.en: You want the child to have an IQ of 65 or 145?

cues.zh: 选吧。
cues.en: Decide.

cues.zh: 好，那你们都要投票……
cues.en: Okay, so you're all going to vote...

cues.zh: 好，你们觉得自己会投票选一个智商65的孩子吗？
cues.en: Okay, you think any one of you is going to vote to have a child with an IQ of 65?

cues.zh: 那个孩子连语言能力的发展都会很困难。
cues.en: That child is going to have a hard time developing even Linguistic ability.

cues.zh: 他们永远学不会阅读。
cues.en: They're never going to learn to read.

cues.zh: 他们永远离不开家
cues.en: They're never going to leave home

cues.zh: ——大概率如此。那你们选哪个孩子？
cues.en: - in all likelihood. So which child are you going to pick?

cues.zh: 那么，你到底相不相信智力这回事？嗯，显然……只要你有脑子……
cues.en: Well, so do you believe in intelligence, or not? Well, obviously... if you have any sense...
